title: Belonging to clubs and societies
summary: Williams lists the social and aid clubs he belongs to, such as the Greyhound club and the Garden District, and talks about funeral parades and the Young Men of Liberty's music.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: But did you belong to many clubs and societies and stuff?

I belonged to the Greyhound, they used to parade too, Greyhound sports. And the Garden District, they used to give a lot of dances and picnics and different things. And while the young man delivered, I was in there, otherwise they used it. Old man Bob, Bob, Bob, he was a member. He died in there, you know. And I'm in there, thirty-some odd years. Thirty-some odd years. Well, it's a constitutional choir for music, buried with music. But we down now to fifty-six. Fifty-six members. But we got plenty of money. So we just put up a fight. And for man, you know, be. Now I belong to another club, the Micah Doodles, they give music too.
Micah Doodles. They meet at Irada, Irada and Clayborne, underneath the bridge.
Well, how long since they've had a band there?
Micah Doodles. About two months ago.
For a funeral? Uh-huh. On a Saturday. I never saw them. I never saw a band with the Liberty either. Satchelor Liberty?
No, with the Liberty Club. Yeah, Young Mons of Liberty?
No, well they had the music.
Now the only way we have that music, in fact, a fella pushing the dial, doubting if they want that music, they have to give it to them. Because they do not pay for that music.
